scope: round invalidated by a design mistake: connected to the dedrun instead of our own server

what_went_wrong.goal: verify that the client adopted the challenge issued by server1649370
what_went_wrong.mistake: the session was started against the 2697 dedrun (target 28970), not against server1649370 on 28971
what_went_wrong.consequence: any challenge read from the client would be the dedrun's, not ours, so the experiment cannot answer the question

why_it_matters: challenge adoption is the leading suspect for why our correctly fragmented gamestate is still not acknowledged: if the client keeps a different challenge than the one we signed, every cipher byte we produce is wrong and no framing fix can help
correct_design_for_next_round: start server319.lsg on 28969 and server1649370.gameserver on 28971
start the client, log in to the lobby
ring-a-drain block, install the refresh hook, start-challenge
read the server's own challenge_assigned from runs/gs*.jsonl
then read the client connection object (CLIENT_SLOT 0x82c3b58 / CLIENT_POINTERS 0x1c1d188 / XOR 0xfbb2c97a per the 1649370 layout.py) and search it for that value
if the value is present, the client adopted our challenge and the cipher is right; if absent, the cipher key source is wrong
note: testing this against the dedrun would only tell us that the dedrun's challenge is adopted, which we already know from the fact that its gamestate reaches phase 8
